newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cannot find cause of poisoning epidemic.
newsitem.headline: Japan cannot find cause of poisoning epidemic.

text.p: Japan's Health Ministry said on Thursday it could not identify the exact source of a food poisoning epidemic that swept across the nation this summer, but still suspects radish sprouts as a possible cause.

The ministry said in its final report on the crisis that it was unable to specify the source and route by which the deadly O-157 bacteria spread, creating one of the biggest health scandals since World War Two.

But the report said there was reason to believe that contaminated radish sprouts, a salad vegetable similar to cress, were the cause of the poisoning from the O-157 E. coli bacillus, which killed 11 people and made more than 9,500 ill.
The western Japan city of Sakai was hit hardest by the epidemic, with more than 6,500 people, mainly schoolchildren, affected. Experts believe the bacteria was in school lunches.
But investigators failed to track down the original source of the bacillus and schools in Sakai stopped supplying school lunches when classes resumed this autumn.
"The government cannot call the epidemic over until all elementary schools resume their lunch programme," chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
A farmer identified by investigators as producing suspected radish sprouts said his company planned to file a damage suit against the central government.
"None of the tests showed our products carried the bacteria. I just can't accept it (the conclusion)," the farmer told reporters.
Parents of children affected by the poisoning in Sakai said earlier this month they would sue the city for damages.
Sakai Mayor Hideo Hataya said on Wednesday he would return part of his salary for the next six months to take responsibility for the outbreak in schools.
Kajiyama said that as of September 20, eight people in Sakai were still in hospital, of whom one was said to be in serious condition.
